name: Eliehoenai
overview: Eliehoenai is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Pahath-moab and the son of Zerahiah. He is noted for having accompanied Ezra during the return to Jerusalem, as recorded in the book of Ezra. No tribal affiliation or additional personal details are provided in Scripture beyond these facts.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliehoenai means 'my eyes [look] to YHWH,' reflecting a devotional focus on the Lord. This proper name, recorded in Ezra 8:4, highlights a spiritual posture of dependence and trust in God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Eliehoenai is the son of Zerahiah. No other family relationships are mentioned beyond what is stated in his unique attribute.
scriptureSignificance: Eliehoenai's significance lies in his role as one of the returnees with Ezra to Jerusalem, demonstrating faithfulness to God's call to restore the community and worship. His lineage as a descendant of Pahath-moab situates him within the broader context of the exilic return, emphasizing God's providential preservation of His people. Through his participation in this pivotal event, Eliehoenai represents those who trusted in God's promises during a time of national restoration.
